text:
Logan Wright: perf test results from last night’s run on the usage-insights top routes query. tl;dr we’re close on p95 but still have a couple sharp edges w/ filter combos + cold cache. dropping numbers + follow-ups here.

Mei Lin: nice. is this the k6 run against staging w/ prod-ish data volume?

Logan Wright: yep. k6 against `staging-console-backend` w/ a snapshot of last week’s aggregates (anonymized). Query under test is `GET /v1/insights/routes` (top spend) with:
- org+project scoping
- time window: 7d + 30d
- group_by: route
- filters toggled: env, region, deployment_mode

Logan Wright: Results (50 RPS sustained, 5 min warmup, 20 min steady):
- 7d window
  - p50: 118ms
  - p95: 410ms
  - p99: 780ms
- 30d window
  - p50: 240ms
  - p95: 980ms
  - p99: 1.9s
- Error rate: 0.0% app errors, but ~0.6% requests exceeded our 2s server timeout on *cold cache* when `region=all` + `deployment_mode=all` (worst case query plan)

Allison Grant: p95 980ms for 30d is fine for GA? what’s the target we wrote into the SLO draft again

Logan Wright: SLO draft for the insights API is p95 < 1.2s at 30d (and <700ms at 7d) for top routes endpoint, so we’re within, but the cold cache tail is what worries me.

Chloe Martin: do we have cache hit rates from the same run? want to know if we’re actually benefiting from the console caching or just lucky dataset

Logan Wright: cache stats during steady state:
- response cache (service-level) hit rate: ~72% (7d) / ~61% (30d)
- redis p95 for `GET`: 2.4ms
- biggest misses are when the UI spams slightly different time ranges (e.g. `now-7d` vs `now-7d+5m`) -> different cache key

Felix Schneider: yeah the UI currently uses “floating now” when you paginate/sort. I can clamp the end_ts to minute boundaries (or use server-provided canonical window) so cache keys don’t explode.

Jada Williams: on the DB side, the cold-cache p99 looked like a plan regression. did we confirm we’re using the composite index in the materialized view for org/project + bucket_start?

Mei Lin: I checked the explain on the slowest sample query from logs — it was doing an index scan but still reading a lot of partitions. The `bucket_start` predicate is not sargable when the API passes `start_time`/`end_time` with seconds; our partitioning is hourly boundaries.

Thomas Baird: +1. also seeing cardinality guardrail kick in at the same time window. when the rollup is invoked (route_hash -> `__other__` bucket), query touches both “raw route” and “rolled up” tables due to how we join for labels.

Nadia Rahman: that join is optional for the top routes view right? for list view we don’t actually need to resolve all labels beyond top N.

Chloe Martin: right now we resolve route display names for all returned rows, but we request `limit=200` for the table (including hidden rows for the sparkline). We could reduce label resolution to `limit` only and make the sparkline request separate.

Felix Schneider: FYI table currently prefetches 200 even if you see 50 on screen bc we wanted smoother sorting. can change.

Allison Grant: can we quantify impact of caching itself? i.e., cold vs warm p95

Logan Wright: yep. cold cache (flush redis) single-shot runs (10 RPS, 5 min):
- 7d p95: 690ms
- 30d p95: 1.65s
- 30d p99: 2.8s (this is where we clip / time out)
Warm cache after 1–2 mins of traffic drops back to the earlier numbers.

Talia Benson: is the cold-cache scenario realistic after deploys? (we’ll restart pods + clear in-memory caches). do we expect redis to persist across deploy?

Logan Wright: redis persists, so only new cache keys are cold. but the “floating now” key churn means effectively cold most of the day for active users. so Felix’s clamp should help a lot.

Jada Williams: another fix: we can canonicalize windows server-side. e.g. for “last_7d” return `window_end` rounded to hour and include it in response so the UI uses the exact same boundaries when re-requesting.

Felix Schneider: that’d be ideal. UI can switch to: request `preset=last_7d` and use `window_end` from response for subsequent calls.

Mei Lin: also, for 30d queries we can route to daily aggregates if the user isn’t looking at hourly granularity. Right now the endpoint always hits hourly because we reuse it for sparklines.

Chloe Martin: we can split endpoints: list view uses daily aggregates + returns daily sparkline points; detail view uses hourly when you drill in.

Allison Grant: careful on freshness messaging though. daily rollup can lag more. but for 30d view, 1-2h lag is fine.

Thomas Baird: from cardinality perspective, pushing list view to daily also reduces partitions touched. should also reduce worst-case when `region=all`.

Grafana Bot: Alert note (staging): `usage-insights-api p95` breached 1.5s for 6m at 09:12 UTC. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/usage-insights-api/overview?var-env=staging (annotation: k6 run)

Logan Wright: follow-up tasks I’m proposing (ties into ENG-8433):
1) Server-side time window canonicalization + cache key normalization (owner: Jada + Logan) — add `window_start/window_end` rounding (hour) + accept `preset` values.
2) UI: stop “floating now”, clamp end_ts, reduce prefetch from 200 -> 50, and split sparkline fetch (owner: Felix)
3) Data: add daily rollup path for list endpoint (owner: Mei) — behind feature flag; confirm freshness behavior.
4) DB: verify/adjust index so `org_id, project_id, bucket_start` is always used; also ensure queries pass bucket-aligned timestamps (owner: Mei + Chloe)
5) Cardinality join optimization: only resolve labels for top N; avoid joining rolled-up table unless needed (owner: Thomas + Nadia)

Chloe Martin: +1. I’ll add a note: we should cap `limit` on the endpoint to 100 in the short term. k6 used 200 and it increases label/join work.

Nadia Rahman: I can take (5) with Thomas. I think we can restructure to:
- query top N route_hash by cost first
- then label lookup for those N only
no reason to label-join the entire intermediate.

Thomas Baird: yep. also want to ensure `__unknown__` bucket stays cheap. right now it’s disproportionately heavy because it’s often top 1 and then triggers a bunch of label resolution.

Allison Grant: what’s the rollback/mitigation if we see the 2.8s p99 in prod? just bump server timeout?

Logan Wright: prefer not to. mitigation plan:
- keep response cache TTL 5m (currently 60s) for list endpoint
- enforce preset windows so cache hit rate increases
- add query timeout at DB level (e.g. 1500ms) and return partial (top routes w/o sparklines) w/ banner (if we can do safely)
We can also temporarily restrict 30d to daily aggregates only.

Chloe Martin: returning partial might be scope creep. I’d rather fail fast with a clear error and have UI retry w/ narrower window. but ok to consider.

Felix Schneider: UI can show: “This report is too large. Try 7d or filter region/env.” if API returns specific error code.

Jada Williams: we already have `QUERY_COST_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` in the API contract draft. we can start using it for worst-case combos.

Talia Benson: can you all link the k6 config + results somewhere I can attach to the weekly update?

Logan Wright: yep. notes + graphs: https://drive.redwood.example/eng/usage-insights/perf/k6-2026-02-09
k6 script PR (internal): https://github.redwood.example/redwood/console-backend/pull/15498

Deploy Bot: staging deploy complete: `console-backend@9f3c1d2` (includes redis TTL change to 300s). Monitors: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/usage-insights-api/overview?var-env=staging

Allison Grant: after TTL=300s deploy, can someone rerun the cold-cache test? want to validate p99 drops.

Logan Wright: will do this afternoon. expecting p99 mostly unchanged on first request but much better over the next few mins; the bigger win comes from canonical windows.

Mei Lin: I’ll open a Linear subtask under ENG-8433 for daily rollups + partition alignment changes.

Chloe Martin: I’ll take the endpoint `limit` cap + label join reduction (pairs with Nadia/Thomas). will post query plan diffs once we have.

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: I’ll update ENG-8433 with these and tag owners.
